title: Red warning light on the dashboard: what to do
metaDesc: A red warning light came on while driving? Which red lights mean pull over and turn the engine off now, and what to do next.
first: Red means act now. Turn on your hazard lights and get fully off the road when it's safe.
Oil can or thermometer light: turn the engine off as soon as you've stopped.
Red BRAKE light: make sure the parking brake is all the way off. If it stays on, don't drive until it's checked.
Battery light: the car can die without warning. Turn off what you don't need and get to a safe place off the road.
A flashing check engine light is just as serious: pull over and turn the engine off.
dont: Don't keep driving just to get home with a red oil, temperature or brake light on.
Never open the radiator cap while the engine is hot.

steps.t: Pull over and turn the engine off right away. Driving even a few miles can wreck the engine. Once it's off, check the oil level. If it's low, add the right oil. If the light stays on, or the level was fine, have it towed.
Pull over and turn the engine off. If you can't stop right away, turn the A/C off and the heater on full hot with the fan on high until you can. Never open the radiator cap while it's hot.
Make sure the parking brake is fully off. If the light stays on, don't drive until it's checked, even if the pedal feels normal. If the pedal feels soft or sinks, have it towed.

The car is running on battery power and can stall without warning. Steering and brakes get much heavier if it does. Turn off the radio, A/C and anything you don't need, and drive only as far as a safe place off the road. Don't try to finish your trip.
This is yellow or orange, but flashing means a bad misfire that can overheat the exhaust and start a fire. Ease off the gas, pull over and turn the engine off.

A red seat belt or door light means buckle up or close the door. A red airbag light means the airbags may not work in a crash, so get it checked soon. Not sure which light it is? Look it up on our warning lights page.

call: If the light's page says don't drive, call your roadside plan or your insurer's roadside line for a tow.
Call 911 if you see smoke or you're stuck in a traffic lane.
